{{Short description|Taiwanese scientist}}
[[File:01.06 總統出席「國家太空中心揭牌典禮」 (52610404304).jpg|thumb|Wu Jong-shinn in 2023]] 
'''Wu Jong-shinn''' ({{zh|t=吳宗信|poj=Gô͘ Chong-sìn}}, also '''Wu Tsung-hsin'''; born 1964) is a Taiwanese scientist, professor, and administrator. He is the director general of the [[Taiwan Space Agency]].

==Early life==
Wu was born in rural [[Tainan]]. His parents were illiterate, and worked in primarily in [[Agriculture in Taiwan|agriculture]], as well as other manual jobs. Wu's first language was [[Taiwanese Hokkien]], and he struggled with the language of instruction, [[Taiwanese Mandarin]], until the second grade. Due to his family's economic status, Wu and his siblings were not provided with opportunities to build [[model rocket]]s, but during [[Lunar New Year]] and [[Mid-Autumn Festival]] celebrations, they set off [[firecracker]]s.<ref name="cnaengprofile">{{cite news |last1=Chung |first1=Yu-chen |title=FEATURE/'Rocket uncle' keeps Taiwan's space dream alive |url=https://focustaiwan.tw/sci-tech/202402100005 |access-date=11 February 2024 |date=10 February 2024 |agency=Central News Agency}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
[[File:國家太空中心衛星操控中心.jpg|thumb|Wu with TASA staff in 2023]]
In 1986 he received a BS in [[mechanical engineering]] from [[National Taiwan University]] and a MS in the same field from the same school in 1988. In 1994 he received a PhD in [[aerospace engineering]] from the [[University of Michigan]]. Upon returning to Taiwan the following year, he went to work for the [[National Space Organization]] and stayed there for two years. In 1998 he joined the faculty of [[National Chiao Tung University]] and has spent his career there becoming a distinguished professor.<ref name="Curriculum Vitae" >{{cite web |title=Prof. Jong-Shinn Wu |url=https://appl.web.nctu.edu.tw/member/prof-jong-shinn-wu/ |website=nctu.edu.tw |publisher=NCTU |access-date=9 August 2021}}</ref><ref name="cnaengprofile"/> 

Wu's work with students led to the first successful test launch of a hybrid rocket in Taiwan, from the Syuhai launch site in [[Mudan, Pingtung]], in 2010. Two years later, he was named the inaugural director of the [[Advanced Rocket Research Center]]. In 2015, while affiliated with the ARRC, Wu gave the first full [[TED (conference)|TEDx Talk]] in Taiwanese Hokkien. The following year, Wu co-founded the space technology company [[TiSPACE]], alongside some former students. Wu's character and career up to this point inspired the [[Mayday (Taiwanese band)|Mayday]] song "Tough", released on the 2016 album ''[[History of Tomorrow]]''. He left TiSPACE in 2018.<ref name="cnaengprofile"/>

His specialization is in [[space systems engineering]], [[hybrid and liquid rocket propulsion]], [[rarefied gas dynamics]], [[low-temperature plasma physics and applications]], and [[parallel scientific computing]].<ref>{{cite news |first1=Chia-nan |last1=Lin |title=New director takes over at space organization |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2021/08/04/2003762007 |work=Taipei Times |access-date=9 August 2021}}</ref>

He is known as “rocket uncle.”<ref name="cnaengprofile"/><ref name="Taiwan News" />

In August 2021 he was appointed to replaced acting National Space Organization director general Yu Hsien-cheng.<ref name="Taiwan News" >{{cite web |last1=Jiang |first1=Sarah |title=Taiwan's 'Rocket Uncle' steps up as director of National Space Organization |url=https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/4264180 |work=Taiwan News |date=4 August 2021 |access-date=4 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |first1=Si-soo |last1=Park |title=University of Michigan graduate named to lead Taiwan's space agency |url=https://spacenews.com/university-of-michigan-graduate-named-to-lead-taiwans-space-agency/ |website=spacenews.com |date=9 August 2021 |publisher=Space News |access-date=9 August 2021}}</ref>

== Awards and fellowships == 
He is an [[American Society of Mechanical Engineers]] (ASME) Fellow, an [[American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics]] (AIAA) Associate Fellow, [[International Academy of Astronautics]] (IAA) Corresponding Member, and [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE) Senior Member. He sits on the Editorial Advisory Board of AIAA Journal, AIAA Hybrid Rocket Technical Committee, and IEEE Emerging Plasma Nanotechnologies (TC 17) Member
